Trigonal planar, because three domains give planar geometry.
Linear, because two bonds remain.
Tetrahedral, because four domains are ideal.

questions.explanation: Three domains with one lone pair give a bent molecular shape, like SO2. The geometry is trigonal planar but shape is bent.
questions.hint: One lone pair bends the shape.

questions.topic: Ideal angle from the domain count
questions.learningObjective: State ideal angle for five domains
questions.stem: An architect's brief needs the ideal angle between equatorial positions in a five-domain geometry; what is it in degrees?
questions.explanation: In trigonal bipyramidal geometry, equatorial positions are 120 degrees apart. Axial-equatorial angles are 90 degrees.
questions.hint: Equatorial positions spread in a plane.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Apply linearity to a known molecule
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief examines BeCl2; with two domains and no lone pairs on beryllium, what is its shape?

options.text: Bent, because chlorine atoms repel.
Trigonal planar, because three atoms are present.
Linear, because two domains oppose.
Tetrahedral, because beryllium expands its octet.

questions.explanation: BeCl2 has two domains and no lone pairs on beryllium, giving a linear shape. Beryllium is an exception to the octet rule.
questions.hint: Two domains, no lone pairs: linear.

questions.learningObjective: Predict ionic vs covalent from elements
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief pairs sodium with chlorine; what bond type forms?

options.text: Covalent, because both are small atoms.
Hydrogen, because salt water contains H.
Metallic, because sodium is a metal.
Ionic, because a metal meets a nonmetal.

questions.explanation: Sodium is a metal and chlorine is a nonmetal, so they form an ionic bond through electron transfer. Metal plus nonmetal means ionic.

questions.learningObjective: Explain electron sharing in covalent bonds
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief asks why two hydrogen atoms form a covalent bond; which reason is correct?

options.text: Because sharing one pair gives each atom a stable duet.
Because hydrogen atoms transfer electrons to become H+ and H-.
Because a sea of electrons forms between them.
Because hydrogen bonds link the two atoms.

questions.explanation: Sharing lets both atoms achieve a stable duet without transferring charge. This is the simplest covalent case.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate relative attraction from charges and distance
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief gives two ionic pairs both with charges +1 and -1; if one distance is half the other, how many times stronger is its attraction?
questions.explanation: Coulomb attraction scales as 1/r, so halving the distance quadruples the attraction. The factor is 4.

questions.learningObjective: Write a neutral formula from ions
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief needs a neutral compound from Na+ and O2-; what is the formula?

options.text: NaO, because one of each balances.
Na2O2, because doubling both is safer.
NaO2, because oxygen needs two sodiums reversed.
Na2O, because two +1 balance one -2.

questions.explanation: Two Na+ ions (+2 total) balance one O2- (-2), giving Na2O. Charge magnitudes determine the ratio.

Square planar, because four bonds are visible.

questions.explanation: Six electron domains give octahedral geometry. Square planar is a molecular shape derived from it, not the geometry.

T-shaped, because three lone pairs create a T.
Trigonal planar, because three lone pairs spread.
options.misconception: confuses lone pair geometry with shape

options.text: Linear, because the two bonds are 180 degrees apart.

questions.explanation: In XeF2, the two bonding domains are opposite each other (180 degrees), giving a linear molecular shape despite five total domains.
